title: Model behavior
intro: Examine accuracy, uncertainty and whether behavior transfers to the intended setting.
action: Evaluate representative cases and failure modes, inspect uncertainty and compare with a baseline.

items.title: Hallucination
items.meaning: AI generates false or misleading answers.

items.title: Bias
items.meaning: Systematic errors or skew in data, modeling or measurement can distort outcomes; bias is not always unintentional and is not identical to every fairness concern.

items.title: Model Drift
items.meaning: Model performance or the relationship between inputs and outcomes can change; degradation is not necessarily gradual.

items.title: Underfitting
items.meaning: Model fails to learn useful patterns.

items.title: Uncertainty
items.meaning: A system may present an answer more confidently than the evidence supports. A numeric score is not automatically a calibrated uncertainty estimate.

title: Data and privacy
intro: Protect the quality, permissions and lifecycle of information used by the system.
action: Record provenance and permissions, control access and retention, and check data quality and leakage.

items.title: Duplicate Data
items.meaning: Uncontrolled duplicates can distort sampling and leak information across evaluation splits; deliberate reweighting serves a different purpose.

items.title: Synthetic Data Risk
items.meaning: Generated data can reproduce errors, omit relevant variation or create feedback effects. Its quality depends on generation and evaluation, rather than being poor simply because it is synthetic.

items.title: Consent Risk
items.meaning: A dataset may lack required permission or another appropriate basis for the intended use; obligations depend on context.

items.title: Data Leakage
items.meaning: Information may enter training or evaluation that would be unavailable in real use, or private data may be exposed. Distinguish these two failure modes.

title: Security and tool authority
intro: Treat model inputs as untrusted and enforce permissions in the surrounding software.
action: Restrict credentials and tool permissions, validate operations and enforce execution limits outside the model.

items.title: Adversarial Attack
items.meaning: Inputs are designed to fool models.

title: Governance and accountability
intro: Make ownership, requirements, review and evidence explicit.
action: Assign owners, record the applicable requirements, document decisions and create escalation and review paths.

items.title: Ownership Gap
items.meaning: No clear person owns AI outcomes.

items.title: Explainability Gap
items.meaning: People may lack a useful account of how an output was produced, its evidence or its limitations. Explanations must suit the decision and audience.

items.title: Metric Blindness
items.meaning: Teams track the wrong AI metrics.

title: Operations and business value
intro: Assess reliability, recovery, cost and the value of the whole workflow.
action: Measure end-to-end outcomes and costs, set limits and alerts, and test recovery before relying on the workflow.

items.title: Vendor Lock-In
items.meaning: Business depends too much on one provider.

items.title: Feedback Gap
items.meaning: User feedback never improves the system.

title: People and social effects
intro: Examine how the system changes decisions, trust, work and outcomes for affected people.
action: Seek affected-user input, assess group impacts and provide meaningful review, challenge and redress.

items.title: Misuse Risk
items.meaning: A system may be used outside its intended or permitted purpose, with consequences for affected people.
